clue.text: Advertising medium for port administrators

parts.note: Sandwich is one of the Cinque Ports on the Kent coast
a board is a body of people who run an organisation

explanation.surface: A Kent harbour's managers are presented as a publicity outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent, England, and one of the historic Cinque Ports, so 'port' does not have to mean a drink or the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of placards hung front and back on a person who walks the streets is a traditional way of carrying adverts.

clue.text: Monotonous studies — no glory involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A complaint that academic work brings tedium and no fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' tells you to rearrange STUDIES, NO and GLORY together; the dash is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Work so dull that it crushes the spirit is described with this hyphenated adjective, a near synonym of tedious.

clue.text: It cures, but can upset soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for can is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a can is a tin
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Something is a remedy but may also unsettle the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It cures' means it preserves meat, not that it heals; saltpetre has long been used to cure bacon and ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre (potassium nitrate) is a traditional curing agent for preserved meats.

clue.text: Retirement from the bank?

parts.note: retirement suggests someone leaving a job at a bank, but it is money being taken out of an account

explanation.surface: A banker stepping down from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking cash out of an account is the usual banking term, and the same word also means retreating or pulling back.

clue.text: Company in which old city accountant swallows a liqueur

indicators.note: the word for company has the rest placed in it
the old city and the accountant together take in the single letter between them

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A firm where an ancient town's bookkeeper drinks a cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the Sumerian city of Abraham, is the crossword's favourite 'old city'; 'swallows' and 'in which' are both containers, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-flavoured spirit, named after a Caribbean island, is a well-known after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Base in France, or in Arabia, for this wanderer

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a flower bed or the bed of a road
ou is the French word for or
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller is said to have a home base in France or in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' qualifies the word after it, asking for the French translation; the second 'in' is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: These Arab desert people are traditionally nomadic, moving their tents and herds from place to place.

clue.text: Chief misses beginning of demonstration

indicators.note: the word for demonstration loses its opening letter

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A leader fails to turn up at the start of a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective or prefix it means principal, as in arch-enemy or archbishop.

clue.text: Beryllium used in plate for security

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is placed inside the word for plate

parts.note: a dental plate is a denture
Be is the chemical symbol for beryllium

explanation.surface: A metal element is employed in making a sheet of armour for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like metal sheeting, but it is the dental kind holding false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond issued by a company and backed by its assets is a form of financial security.

clue.text: Lack of influence of space explorers?

definitions.text: Lack of influence of space explorers?

parts.words: Lack of influence of space explorers?
parts.note: a lack of influence would be having no weight to throw around, which literally describes astronauts floating in orbit

explanation.surface: Astronauts are mocked for having no clout.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no weight is the state of floating free of gravity, and weight is also a word for influence.

clue.text: Lacking education, turned to university for amendment

indicators.note: the letters are to be amended, that is changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone without schooling went to a university to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'for amendment' tells you to rearrange TURNED TO plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has never been taught has had no schooling.

clue.text: Rope reaching much further than a chain

definitions.meaning: a thick strong rope, such as a ship's anchor line

definitions.text: reaching much further than a chain
definitions.meaning: as a nautical measure this length, a tenth of a sea mile, is far longer than a chain of 22 yards

explanation.surface: A line is boasted to stretch beyond any metal links.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old British length of 22 yards; the nautical unit meant here is about 200 yards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a heavy mooring line and a sailors' unit of distance much longer than the surveyor's chain.

clue.text: Greatly fear being late to receive king

indicators.note: the word for late takes in the abbreviation for king

parts.note: the late means dead
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified of turning up after a monarch arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, as in 'the late Mr Smith', not overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be terrified of something is to anticipate it with great anxiety.

clue.text: Bludgeon the driver, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to beat with a heavy stick
a golfer's driver is one example of the stick used to hit the ball

explanation.surface: Beating up a chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is not a motorist: it is the golf stick used for long shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy stick is a cudgel, and each of a golfer's sticks bears the same name.

clue.text: Difficulty Siegfried initially encountered with a horse

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Wagner's hero meets trouble when he comes upon a steed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch or unexpected obstacle is a problem that holds things up.

clue.text: In status he is treated as a devotee

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of the three words are reworked

explanation.surface: A man of high standing is regarded as a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen fan or zealous follower of something is passionately devoted to it.

clue.text: A superior performer in the Nuns' Chorus

definitions.text: A superior performer in the Nuns' Chorus

parts.words: A superior performer in the Nuns' Chorus
parts.note: superior suggests the Mother Superior of a convent, but it means the singer of the highest part in an all-female choir

explanation.surface: Praise for an outstanding singer in a convent choir.
explanation.walkthrough: In a choir of women's voices, the highest part is the top one, so the 'superior' performer is the one singing above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This voice sings the highest line in a choir, above the altos.

clue.text: Take fright about, say, your speech of praise

indicators.note: the word for take fright goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: to panic is to take fright
eg (for example) is a crossword staple for say
yr is the written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: An instruction to get scared of, for instance, your own tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, with the panic word wrapped round both short abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal oration or written piece lavishing praise on someone is a eulogy.

clue.text: Stoppage unions organised before the end of August

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters of the word unions are put in a new order
only the final letter of the month is taken

explanation.surface: Trade unions call a strike set for late summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' signals the anagram of the trade-union word, and 'before' merely places it ahead of the month's last letter. The answer is a legal term for a dismissed case.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the dismissal of a lawsuit because the plaintiff cannot make out a case halts the action.

clue.text: Senior Aircraftman in status has rifle

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for status

parts.note: rank is position or standing
SAC is the RAF abbreviation for Senior Aircraftman

explanation.surface: A junior RAF airman of some standing carries a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is a verb meaning to search through and plunder, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to go through it hastily, looting as you search.

clue.text: Chap accommodating popular sergeant-major's relations

indicators.note: the man's name provides room for the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Ken is a man's name, standing for any chap
in means fashionable or popular
SM is the abbreviation for sergeant-major

explanation.surface: A man puts up the well-liked senior NCO's family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' is the container: the man's name houses both abbreviations. Using a common first name for 'chap' is a standard crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Male relatives by blood are members of the same family.

clue.text: A hindrance circumvented by the sprinter, perhaps

indicators.note: circumvented means gone around, so the second word surrounds the first

parts.note: a let is an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: An obstacle is dodged by a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumvented by' is the container: the article goes round the tennis-style obstacle, as in 'let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is one kind of track-and-field competitor, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: It controls the balance of flyers in a bank

definitions.text: It controls the balance of flyers in a bank

parts.words: It controls the balance of flyers in a bank
parts.note: the balance and the bank sound financial, but this is a hinged flap that keeps an aircraft level and makes it tilt in a turn

explanation.surface: Something manages the account balances of pilots at a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged flap on a wing's trailing edge is what tilts a plane into a banked turn.

clue.text: Ascetic system bringing unknown past back

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: back means the word for past is read in reverse

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A discipline that revives a mysterious history.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hindu discipline of meditation, breathing and posture aims at self-control and spiritual union.

clue.text: Dye obtained from Manila

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken from within the name of the city

explanation.surface: A colouring that comes from the Philippine capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo, a blue colouring made from a West Indian shrub, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Countrymen have a sleeping-place on board

indicators.note: the steamship letters have the bed placed inside them

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for being aboard a vessel
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Fellow nationals are given a bunk aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on board' is conventionally shown by putting something inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Scotland are fellow nationals of one country.

clue.text: Old fellow on island is an Arab

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An elderly man living on an isle comes from the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a sultanate in the south-east of the Arabian peninsula is an Arab.

clue.text: Head of Radio abandons plan for informal talk

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the word for plan

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is wanted

explanation.surface: The chief of a broadcaster drops a scheme in favour of a casual conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Radio' looks like a BBC boss; it is just the letter R, which 'abandons' removes from CHART.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, casual conversation is a natter.

clue.text: A point made by the prime minister

definitions.meaning: one of the four cardinal points of the compass
Lord ... was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: The PM makes an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North, prime minister during the American War of Independence, is the man meant; 'point' is a compass point, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass direction and the name of an 18th-century British premier.

clue.text: Preserve, or ruin, youth in West?

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: the boy is placed inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A question of whether to save or spoil a young man out West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but the Hollywood actress Mae West, giving MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus jam, typically of Seville oranges, is a preserve spread on toast.

clue.text: Some rope given by the Censor in a silent representation

parts.note: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and is known by that title

indicators.note: a representation presents the letters of the three words in another form

explanation.surface: A Roman magistrate offers a length of cord in a mime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' signals rearranging the three words. Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman famous as 'the Censor'; the whip's cords make it 'some rope'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old naval whip was made of knotted cords, so it is literally a bit of rope.
